bibliographic.title: A Five-Layer Framework for AI Governance: Integrating Regulation, Standards, and Certification
bibliographic.venue: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
bibliographic.citation_apa: Agarwal, A., & Nene, M. J. (2025). A five-layer framework for AI governance: Integrating regulation, standards, and certification. Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy, 19(3), 535–555. https://doi.org/10.1108/TG-03-2025-0065

methodology.method_family: framework development with illustrative case studies
methodology.study_design: Five-layer conceptual AI governance framework validated through two case studies on AI fairness and AI incident reporting
methodology.sample_description: Two illustrative case studies (AI fairness; AI incident reporting); no empirical participant or organizational sample described in provided text
methodology.sector: telecom, healthcare, finance, transportation, defense, public services
methodology.technology_context: Broad AI governance spanning regulation, standards, assessment, and certification; references machine learning, NLP, LLMs, and conversational AI in standards context

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article's primary contribution is a general five-layer AI governance framework linking regulation, standards, assessment, and certification, validated via fairness and incident-reporting case studies. It addresses regulated/high-stakes sectors and compliance/risk themes relevant to the review, but LLMs and conversational systems appear as secondary extensions or illustrative regulatory/standards examples rather than as the central object of conversational governance analysis.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Extracted metadata lists year 2023 and preprint type, but front matter indicates 2025 journal publication; conversational AI and LLM relevance is peripheral and requires human confirmation of fit for central versus supporting evidence.

appraisal.notes: Clear conceptual objective and appropriate framework-plus-case-study design for normative governance mapping. Limited transparency in provided excerpts on case-study selection criteria, detailed methods, and explicit study limitations. No primary empirical sampling; validation is illustrative rather than systematically evaluated.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is internally coherent and clearly links regulatory mandates to standards, assessment, and certification. Adequacy for answering conversational-LLM governance questions is partial because conversational AI and LLMs are referenced mainly as standards/extension examples. Confidence is moderate due to illustrative case-study validation and limited methodological detail in the supplied text.

coding.subtheme: Integrating regulation, standards, assessment, and certification
rq_alignment: standards and certification for trustworthy AI

synthesis.main_claim: A five-layer AI governance framework can bridge high-level regulatory mandates and practical implementation through progressively focused layers of standards, assessment procedures, and certification.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a structured roadmap from regulation to certification and uses fairness and incident-reporting case studies to identify governance gaps such as missing standardized assessment and reporting mechanisms.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text emphasizes conceptual mapping and illustrative case studies; conversational AI and LLM governance are not the primary analytic focus. Limitations of the framework's empirical validation are not clearly detailed in the supplied excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for layered governance models, compliance/risk pathways, and standards-based operationalization in regulated sectors; cite cautiously for conversational-LLM governance unless supplemented by sections explicitly analyzing chatbots, agents, or LLM-specific controls.
